transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

I came in because I’m barely sleeping in any useful way anymore. I lie awake replaying client models, and then I wake up around three or four with my stomach all tight. I go to work feeling like I never really rested at all.
Aside from the sleep difficulties, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless most days?
Yes. Most days I feel this heavy, gray sadness, like I’m just going through the motions at work and at home. Sometimes someone asks me a normal question and I have to try not to cry.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you usually enjoy?

Yes. I’ve stopped going to the volunteer teaching, yoga, and book club—I used to really value those. Now I just don’t show up. Even at work, my models and presentations have been slipping enough that I got a formal performance warning.
About how long have you been feeling this way continuously?
About three years now—since the merger reorganized our Caribbean-market division.
During these past three years, have you ever had a period of two months or longer where you felt completely back to your normal self?
No, I haven’t had a stretch like that. It’s been there pretty continuously for about three years, since the merger reorganized our Caribbean-market division.
How have your energy levels been over this time—do you find yourself feeling unusually tired or drained?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close attention to my energy levels specifically.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight over this time?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really noticed or kept track of any changes in my appetite or weight.
How have you been feeling about yourself lately—have you noticed a drop in your self-confidence or feelings of inadequacy?
Yes. When a manager questions one of my projections, I immediately take it as proof that I’m not as sharp as I used to be—that everyone can see I’m failing.
